stem: A nurse is connecting a client's hemodialysis central venous catheter for treatment. Which infection-prevention practice is required?

options.A: Use aseptic catheter-access technique and disinfect the catheter hubs with an appropriate antiseptic before access
options.B: Use clean nonsterile technique because aseptic technique is needed only when the catheter is first inserted
options.C: Skip hub disinfection when the catheter cap appears visibly clean
options.D: Reserve aseptic technique for scheduled dressing changes and use routine handling for dialysis connections

rationale: CDC dialysis infection-prevention guidance requires adherence to aseptic technique when connecting and disconnecting hemodialysis catheters and during dressing changes. Catheter hubs should be scrubbed with an appropriate antiseptic after the cap is removed and before access, every time the catheter is accessed or disconnected. Maximal sterile barrier precautions are an insertion procedure standard and should not be incorrectly generalized to every routine catheter access. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Use aseptic technique and appropriate catheter-hub disinfection every time a hemodialysis central venous catheter is connected, disconnected, or otherwise accessed.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Best Practices for Bloodstream Infection Prevention in Dialysis Setting
source_version_date: CDC Dialysis Safety page dated 2024-03-29; current content accessed 2026-08-17; CDC Dialysis Component reviewed 2026-01-16
source_locator: Catheter/vascular access care observations: assess adherence to aseptic technique when connecting/disconnecting catheters and during dressing changes. Catheter hub disinfection: scrub hubs with appropriate antiseptic after cap removal and before accessing; perform every time catheter is accessed or disconnected
source_claim_supported: Hemodialysis catheter connection/disconnection and dressing care require aseptic technique, with hub disinfection before each access/disconnection.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

correction_summary: Replaced the source item's imprecise statement that 'strict sterile technique' is required for every tunneled-catheter access with CDC's exact requirement for aseptic access technique and hub disinfection. Distinguished routine access from maximal sterile barrier precautions used at insertion.
audit_findings: A is directly supported. B and D incorrectly limit aseptic technique to insertion/dressing only; C omits mandatory hub disinfection based on appearance. No second answer, terminology overreach, or unsupported dressing frequency remains. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
